Copying a reference does not copy its object. Two variables can refer to the same mutable object.
Draw boxes for objects and arrows for references. Reassigning one variable changes its arrow; modifying an object is visible through every alias.
int[] a={1,2}; int[] b=a; b[0]=9; System.out.println(a[0]);
Java passes every argument by value, including reference values.
A method can mutate an object reached through a copied reference. Assigning a different object to its parameter does not reassign the caller's variable.
int n=3; int copy=n; copy=8; System.out.println(n);
An invariant describes the valid states of an object and should hold at public method boundaries.
Keep representation fields private. Validate constructor arguments and reject updates that break the invariant. Returning an internal mutable array can expose the representation.
int balance=10; int withdrawal=4; if(withdrawal>=0 && withdrawal<=balance) balance-=withdrawal; System.out.println(balance);
An immutable object's observable state does not change after construction.
Final fields prevent reassignment, but a final reference can still point to a mutable object. Copy mutable inputs and avoid exposing mutable internal state.
int[] original={2,4}; int[] copy=original.clone(); copy[0]=8; System.out.println(original[0]);
The == operator compares reference identity, while equals can express logical equality.
Override equals consistently with reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, consistency, and null handling. A class that overrides equals should also override hashCode.
String a=new String("java"); String b=new String("java"); System.out.println(a.equals(b));
Equal objects must have equal hash codes; unequal objects may share a hash code.
A hash table uses hashing to narrow the candidate bucket and equality to identify the key. Avoid mutating equality-relevant fields while an object is a key.
java.util.Set<String> s=new java.util.HashSet<>(); s.add(new String("x")); s.add(new String("x")); System.out.println(s.size());
Overridden instance methods dispatch according to the runtime class of the receiver.
The declared type controls which members can be called at compile time. Overloading is resolved at compile time; overriding chooses an implementation at runtime.
An interface describes a contract that multiple implementations can satisfy.
Program against List or Map when implementation details are unnecessary. Choose implementations using required operations, ordering, null policy, and performance needs.
java.util.List<Integer> xs=new java.util.ArrayList<>(); xs.add(7); xs.add(3); System.out.println(xs.get(1));
Generics express relationships between types and catch incompatible uses at compile time.
A List<Integer> is not a List<Number>. A producer accepting ? extends Number can provide Numbers, but arbitrary Numbers cannot safely be added to it.
java.util.List<String> xs=new java.util.ArrayList<>(); xs.add("type safe"); System.out.println(xs.get(0));
Exceptions communicate failures that callers may handle or propagate.
Use specific exceptions for violated preconditions. Try-with-resources closes resources reliably. A finally block can run even when an exception interrupts the normal path.
A recursive computation needs a base case and progress toward that base case.
Identify a nonnegative measure that decreases on each recursive call. State the subproblem contract before tracing the stack. Each invocation has its own local variables.
int result=1; for(int n=5;n>0;n--) result*=n; System.out.println(result);
Binary search repeatedly discards half of a sorted search interval.
Use a consistent interval convention such as [lo, hi). Preserve the invariant that any matching element remains inside the interval. An empty interval ends the search.
int[] a={2,4,6,8,10}; int lo=0,hi=a.length; while(lo<hi){int m=lo+(hi-lo)/2;if(a[m]<7)lo=m+1;else hi=m;} System.out.println(lo);
Big O describes an asymptotic upper bound on a function's growth.
Specify the input size and cost model. Separate worst-case, expected, and amortized guarantees. Constant factors matter in practice even when asymptotic bounds match.
int count=0; for(int i=0;i<4;i++) for(int j=0;j<4;j++) count++; System.out.println(count);
Geometric capacity growth gives dynamic-array append amortized constant time.
A resize copies the current elements and costs linear time. Across a long sequence of appends, the geometric series of copy costs is linear in the number of appended elements.
java.util.ArrayList<Integer> a=new java.util.ArrayList<>(); for(int i=0;i<5;i++) a.add(i*i); System.out.println(a.get(4));
A linked list represents sequence order through links between nodes.
Update links carefully and handle empty lists, head changes, and tail changes. Insertion is constant time when the relevant node is already known; locating that node may be linear.
java.util.LinkedList<Integer> a=new java.util.LinkedList<>(); a.add(2); a.addFirst(1); a.addLast(3); System.out.println(a.removeFirst());
A stack processes elements in last-in, first-out order.
Use a Deque as a stack. In delimiter matching, store unmatched opening delimiters, match every closing delimiter against the top, and require an empty stack at the end.
java.util.Deque<Integer> s=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>(); s.push(1); s.push(2); System.out.println(s.pop());
A queue processes elements in first-in, first-out order.
Use offer and poll on an ArrayDeque for ordinary queues. Breadth-first exploration uses a queue to process discovered work in increasing distance from the start.
java.util.Queue<Integer> q=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>(); q.offer(1); q.offer(2); System.out.println(q.poll());
Tree traversal applies a recursive computation to each subtree.
Preorder visits the root before children, inorder visits between left and right subtrees, and postorder visits after children. A full traversal takes linear time in the number of nodes.
int[] inorder={1,3,5,7}; for(int x:inorder) System.out.print(x); System.out.println();
A binary search tree orders keys so that left and right subtrees obey an ordering invariant.
Choose and document a duplicate-key policy. Search takes time proportional to height: a balanced tree is logarithmic, while a skewed tree can be linear.
A binary min-heap keeps each parent no greater than its children.
The heap property guarantees a minimum at the root, not globally sorted iteration. Insertion and removing the minimum restore the invariant along one root-to-leaf path.
Collisions occur when different keys map to the same bucket.
Chaining and open addressing resolve collisions differently. Expected constant-time operations depend on suitable hashing and controlled load; worst-case guarantees may differ.
A stable sort preserves the relative order of elements that compare as equal.
Comparator ordering should be consistent and transitive. Prefer Integer.compare to subtraction, since subtraction can overflow and violate ordering expectations.
Merge sort combines sorted subproblems by repeatedly choosing the smallest remaining front element.
Balanced splitting has logarithmic depth and each merge level processes linear total work, giving O(n log n) time. Standard array merge sort needs auxiliary storage.
An adjacency list stores the neighbors of each vertex explicitly.
Adjacency lists use O(V+E) space. An adjacency matrix uses O(V squared) space and supports direct edge lookup. Choose using density and the required operations.
Breadth-first search finds shortest path lengths in an unweighted graph.
Mark vertices when enqueuing them to avoid repeated discovery. Store a predecessor for path reconstruction. A traversal with adjacency lists costs O(V+E).
Depth-first search explores an unfinished path before backtracking.
In a directed graph, distinguish unseen, active, and finished vertices. An edge to an active vertex detects a directed cycle; an edge to a finished vertex alone does not.
Boundary tests exercise the transitions where algorithm behavior changes.
Include empty inputs, singleton inputs, duplicates, missing values, and extreme values. Test a contract with independent examples instead of reproducing implementation logic.
An iterator represents a traversal position and may support removal of the last returned element.
For collections that support it, iterator.remove avoids directly modifying the collection during iteration. Fail-fast detection is a bug detector rather than a concurrency guarantee.
